basis: The printing heads this block 'VERS. 24-25.' and it opens 'VERS. 24-25.-- Dixit autem Deus: Producat terra animam viventem, et reliqua, usque et'. The chapter is Migne's caput, carried from the last one the printing states, and the lemma raises nothing against it.
date_basis: Angelomus was a monk of Luxeuil in the middle of the ninth century and wrote for the Emperor Lothar I, who reigned from 840 to 855 and whom the verse prooemium addresses. The Genesis commentary is placed with his commentaries on Kings and on the Song of Songs in that decade. The wiki header gives the eleventh century, which is a century and a half out and is not followed. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1852 printing.
text: VERS. 24-25.-- Dixit autem Deus: Producat terra animam viventem, et reliqua, usque et vidit Deus quod esset bonum. Si enim Deus vidit quod esset bonum, quid dicendum de putredine arborum et infirmitatibus diversarum creaturarum? nisi quoniam cum creata sunt, non apparebant istae infirmitates, sed in sua origine acceperunt ut in futuro haberent. Sed quid est quod ait: Vidit Deus quod esset bonum, id est in ea bonitate placuit ut maneret, in qua placuit ut fieret quod fecit. Sequitur:
